what_its_for: Pentosan polysulfate is used to treat bladder pain and discomfort caused by a condition called interstitial cystitis (IC). It helps protect the lining of your bladder, which may reduce pain, pressure, and the urgent need to urinate frequently.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water. Take it on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before meals or 2 hours after meals. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg taken 3 times a day (for a total of 300 mg per day). Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in a tightly closed container. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other blood-thinning medicines unless your doctor approves, because pentosan polysulfate can increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase this risk as well. Tell your doctor before having any surgery or dental procedures, since this medicine may affect blood clotting.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: unusual bruising or bleeding anywhere on your body, blood in your urine or stool, changes in your vision (such as blurred vision, difficulty reading, or seeing dark spots), hair loss that is noticeable or upsetting, severe stomach pain, signs of liver problems (yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness), or any allergic reaction (rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing).
when_it_works: Pentosan polysulfate works slowly. Most patients do not notice improvement until they have been taking it for at least 3 to 6 months. Some people may need up to 6 months of regular use before feeling significant relief. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you do not feel better right away.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. It is not clearly established as safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Older adults: Use with caution, as the risk of bleeding may be higher. Children: The safety and effectiveness in children have not been established. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
